consensus_findings.description: Critical: The plan's mode mapping is inverted relative to the ri-08 RPC it delegates to. D1/D2 route every live durable transition through `submit` (`try_submit_work` -> `/work/submit` -> `submit_task`) and reserve `reconcile` for resume only. But `submit_task` in agent-coordinator/database/migrations/035_work_queue_projection.sql compares the incoming `transition_sequence` against `work_queue_projection_heads` and returns `{'success':false,'reason':'reconciliation_required'}` whenever `v_seq > v_head_seq` (line 117-119); it only advances the head on the `IF NOT FOUND` first-ever-generation branch (line 107-109). `_apply_transition` increments `state.total_iterations` on every phase change (skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:805), so every generation after the first carries seq = head+1 and is rejected. Only `reconcile_work_projection` upserts the head (035 line 167-170). The result is that a coordinated live run projects generation 1 and then degrades on every subsequent transition, which directly falsifies proposal Acceptance line 34 ('A coordinated live run projects and labels each durable phase generation within one existing kanban poll interval') and spec scenario 'Live phase transition is mirrored'.

Critical: D2 requires the SKILL host to 'call submit immediately after every canonical state write', and the spec adds a scenario asserting host-driven execution projects 'the resulting durable tuple' — but on the real prose+runner.py host there is no writer of `current_phase` for ordinary phase advances, so the projected tuple is stale by construction. `apply-outcome` explicitly never touches `current_phase` (skills/autopilot/scripts/phase_agent.py:1225, runner.py:398-403), `record-state-only-archetype` writes only `phase_archetype` (phase_agent.py:1312-1313), and `runner.py` exposes no transition subcommand (runner.py:377-495). The only host-side writers of `current_phase`/`total_iterations` are `gate-answer`'s edge application (runner.py:271-282) and the ESCALATE parks (runner.py:184-185, 244-245, 264-267, 275-276). SKILL.md prose (line 306-320) says the orchestrator owns the phase sequence but gives it no mechanism to persist it. Projecting after `apply-outcome` would therefore repeatedly re-submit the INIT-era tuple, and the plan never enumerates the canonical write paths it claims to hook.

Critical: The plan assumes the `change:<change_id>` label alone makes the canonical work-queue row visible through the kanban query path, but `POST /issues/list` unconditionally prepends `task_type=eq.issue` to the PostgREST filter (agent-coordinator/src/issue_service.py:314) before applying the label filter (line 328-329). apps/kanban-viz/src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts:69-75 posts only `{labels:[`change:${changeId}`]}`, so a projected row whose `task_type` is anything other than the literal string `issue` is invisible no matter how it is labelled. Neither proposal.md, design.md, contracts/README.md, nor work-packages.yaml ever states the `task_type` the adapter passes to `try_submit_work`/`try_reconcile_work_projection` (both take it as a required argument — coordination_bridge.py:668, 754). Compounding this, `issue_service.update` does not filter on `task_type` (issue_service.py:431, 445), so the label write on a non-issue row returns success and the adapter reports a healthy projection while the board shows nothing. Task 3.3 would fail, and the failure is silent rather than degraded.

Critical: Seam 1 fails — design.md D2/D4 and tasks 1.2/2.3 require `runner.py project-state` after every “canonical state write”, but the plan never names the host-driven writers of projection identity `(change_id, current_phase, total_iterations)`. Verified in `skills/autopilot/scripts/runner.py`: identity-changing durable writes today are `gate-answer` (`_apply_transition` / `enter_escalate` + `save_state`) and the parked `gate-check` escalate path (`enter_escalate` + `save_state`). `apply-outcome` / `record-state-only-archetype` persist loop-state but do not change that tuple (`phase_agent.apply_phase_outcome` explicitly never modifies `current_phase`). Ordinary SKILL.md “transition to …” steps have no `runner.py` transition command, so `project-state --mode submit` has no unambiguous attachment point for the phase generations kanban must show.

Critical: Seam 2/8 overclaim — specs/skill-workflow/spec.md “Coordinator-free tiers stay isolated” and tasks.md 1.3 require zero coordination-bridge imports, availability probes, or queue requests for local-parallel/sequential Autopilot. That is unimplementable as written: `skills/autopilot/scripts/phase_agent.py` eagerly `import coordination_bridge` (line 57) and `runner.py` imports `phase_agent` for every host CLI path; `SKILL.md` also runs `check_coordinator.py` before tier selection and `build-dispatch` resolves archetypes through the bridge. Absolute “zero imports/probes” will false-fail against status quo unless narrowed to the new projection publisher.

Critical: The scenario 'Coordinator-free tiers stay isolated' requires that in local-parallel/sequential tiers 'no coordination-bridge import, availability probe, or queue request SHALL occur', and task 1.3 promises regressions proving it. That is already false in the current tree, independent of this change, so the task can only be satisfied by a vacuous test or by unscoped refactoring. `skills/autopilot/scripts/phase_agent.py:57` imports `coordination_bridge` at module scope, and `skills/autopilot/scripts/runner.py:46` imports `phase_agent` — so every `runner.py` invocation in every tier imports the bridge. Worse, the probe happens too: `record_state_only_archetype` calls `coordination_bridge.try_resolve_archetype_for_phase` (phase_agent.py:1297-1298) and `build-dispatch` does the same (phase_agent.py:335), each of which runs `detect_coordination()` inside `_execute_single_endpoint_operation` (coordination_bridge.py:530). SKILL.md invokes `record-state-only-archetype` for INIT unconditionally (SKILL.md:167-170) and runs `gate-check` at step 0 regardless of tier.

Nit: D6 asserts 'repeated updates are set-idempotent' for the `change:<change_id>` label, but the only available write is a whole-list replace. `try_issue_update` forwards `labels` verbatim (coordination_bridge.py:1283-1284) and `issue_service.update` assigns `data['labels'] = labels` wholesale (issue_service.py:420-421) — there is no add-label operation. Passing `['change:<id>']` is idempotent only in the sense that it always ends with exactly that one label; it silently drops any other label the row carries. That matters because other producers label the same table's rows for the same change: openspec/specs/coordinator-task-status-renderer/spec.md:148 documents `/implement-feature` applying `wp:<id>` through `try_issue_update(labels=...)`, and apps/kanban-viz derives repo grouping from a `repo:` label (apps/kanban-viz/src/lib/__tests__/derive-issue-repo.test.ts:64). The plan specifies no read-before-write and no concurrent-writer semantics.

Nit: The crash/resume scenario claims reconciliation leaves 'exactly one canonical, change-labelled row', but the kanban query surface has no status filter and a hard row cap, so past generations stay on the board and the current one can be evicted. `IssueListRequest.status` defaults to `None` (agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py:255) and `list_issues` applies a status filter only when status is truthy (issue_service.py:316-318), so rows that `reconcile_work_projection` sets to `status='cancelled'` (035_work_queue_projection.sql:178-186) are still returned. The query orders `priority.asc,created_at.asc` with `limit=50` (issue_service.py:331-332, default limit 50 at coordination_api.py:260), and useCoordinator.ts:75 sends neither status nor limit. Since the projected phase rows are created last at equal priority, once a change accumulates 50 rows carrying `change:<id>` — one per phase generation, plus the per-task issue rows the coordinator-task-status-renderer already creates for the same change — the newest generation is the first to fall outside the window, which is exactly the row the acceptance criterion depends on.

Nit: Seam 6 labeling is underspecified against the real issue API. design.md D1/D6 says idempotently ensure `change:<change_id>` via `try_issue_update` with set-idempotent repeats, but `agent-coordinator/src/issue_service.py` `update(..., labels=...)` documents and implements full label array replace. A naive `labels=[f"change:{change_id}"]` is only safe while the row’s labels stay empty; the plan never requires read-merge-write (`try_issue_show` → union → `try_issue_update`) or an add-label helper.

Nit: D1 delegates canonical-row labelling to 'existing `try_issue_update`' without pinning the backend, but that helper is not unconditionally coordinator-bound. `try_issue_update` first calls `_github_issue_dispatch` (coordination_bridge.py:1261-1273), which returns a GitHub-backed result whenever `github_issues.issues_backend()` reports `github` — selected by `COORDINATION_ISSUES_BACKEND=github` or by `COORDINATION_GITHUB_REPO` plus a token (github_issues.py:67-79). In that configuration the coordinator work-queue task UUID returned by submit/reconcile is handed to the GitHub client as an issue identifier, so the `change:<id>` label never reaches the canonical queue row, the projection reports degraded (or falsely ok), and the resume retry described in the failure matrix repeats the same misdirected call every time.

Nit: The failure matrix has no row for a change_id that can never be projected, yet the two identity validators disagree. The projection contract requires `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,127}$` in both the bridge (coordination_bridge.py:734) and the RPC (035_work_queue_projection.sql:88-89 and 150-151), while autopilot accepts `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` (phase_agent.py:777). A change id containing an uppercase letter, underscore, or dot is a legal Autopilot/OpenSpec run whose every projection — submit and reconcile alike — returns `invalid_projection_key`, so resume reconciliation can never repair it and the run is permanently degraded rather than transiently so.

Nit: D3 states 'Every path is `save_state` then projection', which is not true of the code it describes and leaves the reviewer unable to tell which unprojected writes are intentional. In `run_loop` four durable writes bypass projection entirely: the GATE_PENDING park (autopilot.py:1079), the phase-stays branch (1092), the GatePending transition refusal (1120), and the terminal memory-id append (1156). `_GateSession._flush` also persists gate decisions and `pending_gate` outside any projection seam (autopilot.py:481), as does the ESCALATE park in `runner.py` (185). Some of these are legitimately non-phase-changing, but ESCALATE parks and gate-pending states are exactly what an operator watching the board needs to see, and the plan neither lists them nor says they are deliberately unprojected.

Nit: work-packages.yaml `wp-live-integration` `scope.write_allow` includes `apps/kanban-viz/**` while proposal.md Out of Scope and design.md D5 forbid frontend/polling changes and treat existing `/issues/list` as a read-only proof surface (`useCoordinator.ts` posts `{labels:["change:<id>"]}` with default `pollIntervalMs=5000`). That write grant invites accidental UI edits during “kanban proof”.

Nit: design.md D2 (“after every canonical state write”) disagrees with specs/skill-workflow/spec.md (“every durably persisted phase generation” keyed by `(change_id, current_phase, total_iterations)`). Implementers following D2 would project after `apply-outcome` / archetype bookkeeping; following the spec would project only when the identity tuple changes. That ambiguity breaks seam 1’s requirement to name the paths that need post-write projection.

Nit: Seam 3 for the prose host is incomplete. In-process `persist_and_project` already save-then-projects and suppresses projection when `save_state` raises, but host-driven `project-state` is a separate read-only CLI that loads whatever is on disk. design.md D2/D3 and tasks 1.2/2.3 say “after” saves without requiring SKILL.md to gate `project-state` on a successful exit from `gate-answer` / `gate-check` / any future transition writer.

Optional: wp-live-integration's scope does not match its tasks in two directions. Task 4.1 asks it to update 'Autopilot documentation', but its `write_allow` lists only tests, `agent-coordinator/tests/**`, `apps/kanban-viz/**`, the work-queue guide, and the change dir — `skills/autopilot/SKILL.md` is writable only by wp-projection-adapter (line 46), so the Autopilot half of 4.1 is out of scope for the package that owns it. Conversely `apps/kanban-viz/**` is granted write access even though proposal.md:22 puts kanban-viz polling/filter semantics out of scope and task 3.3 says 'do not modify frontend polling', so the package can silently make the board pass its own proof.

FYI: The acceptance criterion is a latency bound ('within one existing kanban poll interval') against a default 5000 ms interval (apps/kanban-viz/src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts:27-28, 136), but each projection is at least two bridge operations (submit/reconcile, then label), and every bridge operation runs `detect_coordination()` before its HTTP request (coordination_bridge.py:530-550). So each durable transition costs up to two capability probes plus two coordinator round trips before the row is board-visible, and the poll itself adds up to a full interval on top. Task 4.1 promises to document latency behavior but no budget is stated anywhere in the plan.

Optional: Task 1.3 / Phase 4 verification mention zero bridge imports/probes but do not prescribe an enforceable proof technique. Without AST import-graph, `sys.modules`, or call-spy assertions, implementations can satisfy “no successful requests” while still importing the bridge or calling `detect_coordination` inside skipped try_* helpers.

Optional: work-packages.yaml `wp-live-integration` verification lists skill suites, coordinator tests, and OpenSpec validate, but tasks.md 4.3 also requires the AST truth-direction invariant, Ruff, context-drift, and scope validation. Those gates are easy to skip at package completion.

FYI: Seam 5’s intended kanban query contract is already present and matches the plan’s label choice: `apps/kanban-viz/src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts` `fetchIssuesForSingleChange` POSTs `/issues/list` with `body: {labels:[\`change:${changeId}\`]}` and defaults `pollIntervalMs=5000`. Work-queue rows share `work_queue.labels` (migration 017), so labeling the canonical task id is the right visibility mechanism.

Resume reconciliation ordering for in-process `run_loop` already matches seam 4: after `load_state`, `persist_and_project(..., mode="reconcile")` runs before the `pending_gate` early-return and before phase work (`skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py`). design.md D2/D3 correctly extend the same order to host-driven `project-state --mode reconcile` before gate handling.

Authority and degradation design is sound for seams 3/6/7: design.md failure matrix and D3/D6 keep loop-state authoritative, treat projection/label failures as degraded observability, reuse ri-08 idempotent submit/reconcile to avoid duplicate rows, and forbid queue responses from mutating `LoopState`. contracts/README.md correctly maps the projection_key fields and marks queue responses observability-only.
